transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mood has been all over the place and I feel constantly revved up and on edge, like I can’t shut myself off. My sister actually brought me in today because everything just got to be too much to handle. I feel completely overwhelmed and like my mind is just running away from me.

When you feel like your mind is running away from you, do you ever feel like you are hearing voices that others don't hear, or do you have beliefs that feel unusually intense or strange to those around you?

Yes, sometimes when I'm alone in my room I hear my uncle calling my name clearly or see shadows, and I've also felt this intense, unshakeable belief that I have a special mission to rescue my family's finances. My family completely brushes it off as unrealistic, but these experiences really only seem to happen when I'm feeling highly revved up and on edge.
Have you experienced periods in the past where you felt deeply depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy for several weeks at a time?

Yes, I've had these heavy, hopeless feelings coming and going for about four months now, and it's gotten much worse recently. When it hits, I completely lose interest in things I love like hiking and hanging out, and I just feel so guilty and like everyone would be better off without me.

During those periods of deep depression and hopelessness you mentioned, did you also experience these voices or intense, unusual beliefs, or did they only occur during the times when you felt revved up and energized?

No, those voices and intense beliefs only happen when I'm in that revved-up, high-energy mode. When my mood crashes into that heavy depression, those strange experiences fade away completely. I'm just left feeling empty, guilty, and exhausted instead.

During those periods of deep depression, did you ever feel so hopeless or worthless that you had thoughts of wanting to end your life, or perhaps felt like your body was moving and thinking much slower than usual?

Yes, I've felt so trapped and guilty that I've thought it would be easier not to wake up, and I've even imagined walking into traffic because I felt everyone would be better off without me. On those heavy days, my body slows down so much that even reaching for change at the register feels like I'm trying to push through mud.

The psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusions) occur exclusively during the manic episode ('revved up' state) and are absent during the depressive episodes, which rules out Schizoaffective disorder and supports a primary mood disorder with mood-congruent or mood-incongruent psychotic features.
